While Spider-Man 2 may be a classic, and Web of Shadows may be more of a "comic book" game, Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered strikes a good middle balance and finds itself ahead of the curve, bringing with it one of the best Spider-Man stories gaming has ever seen. With a vibrant and lively open world, a traversal system to rival Skate, and combat reminiscent of the Arkham series, Spider-Man Remastered is definitely worth the time and money. 
(And for those who might need an incentive to purchase on PC over console, there are some cool mods for this game that add pretty much any suit in Spidey's history to the game.)

What Insomniac has done with Spiderman storytelling is pretty remarkable. In a post Arkham/Rocksteady space, they were able to encapsulate their own unique flavor of what it is that we love about Spiderman and strike a perfect tonal balance of drawing some heightened stylistic design from the comics, while also (and more importantly) grounding the characters with impeccable writing, making me care about each of them deeply. Without spoilers, the Otto Octavius through line in particular was one of the best Spiderman stories I've seen in any medium, which is insane when you think about how many iterations of these characters have existed over the years.

Also this game just feels GOOD. The webslinging travel and combat are very smooth, the progression system was versatile enough to keep me invested and leveling up, and the open world has enough to discover that I was highly tempted to 100% this game long after I had completed the main story.

I remember playing this on console. I never completed it on there because I prefer PC, and boy am I glad that this finally came out. The combat is also up there in terms of its impressiveness; it's incredibly engaging and satisfying if you take the time to learn the combo moves.

I'd say this game is great for people who like high-energy gameplay with a heavy focus on story.
